articleTitle: Integrating YOLO and DG-STGCN Systems for Enhanced Human Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the performance of different systems in the field of human action recognition (HAR), specifically You Only Live Once (YOLO) and Dynamic Group Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolution Network (DG-STGCN), and their integrated systems. YOLO is well known for its fast and accurate object recognition; however, it is unable to directly recognize actions and instead detects them by recognizing whether an object is within the workspace. In contrast, DG-STGCN detects and predicts actions through skeleton recognition, enabling it to recognize human action, but it struggles to distinguish between similar actions. To address these limitations, an integrated system that combines the strengths of both YOLO and DG-STGCN was proposed to enhance the accuracy of action recognition. By conducting experiments on a standardized action recognition dataset, we evaluate the performance of YOLO and DG-STGCN individually and compare it to the performance of the integrated system. The experimental results demonstrated that the integrated system significantly outperforms the individual systems in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Design and Control Algorithm Improvement for Modular Self-Reconfigurable Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Modular Self-Reconfigurable Robot (MSRR) are commonly found in dynamic and complex environments, from environmental exploration to warehousing services. This paper introduces Modular Self-Reconfigurable Robot designed by Chun-Min Lee [1], detailing its design, controller, connection logic, and research results. We also optimize its system and control algorithms. On the system side, we updated the Graphical User Interface (GUI) and added a virtual boundary to make it easier to use and to prevent the modular robot from colliding with the experimental platform and causing damage. In terms of control, we improved the mechanism for the robot's coordinate movement, enabling it to move to specified coordinates at faster speed.

articleTitle: Tactile Animal Breathing Motion Reproducer with Animal Video Viewing Device That Gives Lifelike Sensation of Touching Real Animals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Animal-mimicking robots are widely used as tools for therapy and aid in getting mental relaxation. However, precisely mimicking animal may cause discomfort, such as the uncanny valley effect. Therefore, the minimum factors of animals that can be mimicked by robotic devices and give a lifelike feeling of touching real animals should be clarified. We hypothesized that touching on a device that mimics the breathing of animals and showing a video of a live animal gives a feeling of touching live real animals and provides relaxation to the user. To prove this, we made a simple device mimicking animal breathing. We conducted a controlled experiment with 36 participants over 15 minutes using the device. We showed an animal video and asked participants to touch the breath-mimicking device. We measured subjects' moods using the Temporary Mood Scale and lifelikeness using the Godspeed scale. As a result, we found that the simultaneous experience of watching the animal video and touching a breathing device gives a better lifelike sensation of touching real animals than the cases of either experience. We also found that these positive feelings are given whether the person had animal-keeping experience or not.

articleTitle: Temperature Control for Thermal Vacuum Tests Based on Fuzzy Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to use fuzzy logic to compensate for the temperature difference between the test object and the environment in the thermal vacuum test. By collecting and analyzing the temperature change data under different conditions, a fuzzy logic controller was designed. The input of the fuzzy controller is the temperature difference and the temperature change rate and the output is the adjusted temperature. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively reduce the temperature difference and ensure that the test object reaches the target temperature.

articleTitle: Two-Step Hybridized algorithm of Robust Scheduling for Dealing with Uncertain Processing Time
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Manufacturing industries commonly face the challenge of production environment variance, including equipment performance issues, differences in personnel's skill levels, and difficulty in managing the outsourced processing time. These problems lead to bias between the actual processing time and standard processing time set by the manufacturer. So, planning the production schedules in terms of the current standard processing time, can't effectively adapt to the environmental uncertainties, which result in unstable order completion delivery date, production waste, and processing delays, severely affect the accuracy and stability of scheduling. To solve this issue, this research proposes a type of robust scheduling method that take the processing time variability into consideration, to deal with normal variations in manufacturing industries' production environment. This method incorporates the consideration of unstable processing time factors based on optimized scheduling. By simulating large number of possibilities of processing scenarios, and combining with Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO), in a phased approach, optimizes the dual key performance indicators such as Relative Penalty Cost (RC) and Relative Average Makespan Variance (RMV). Through experimentation, it has proven that this technology in simulated and actual data, comparing with only considering deterministic schedule of standard processing time, the on-time delivery rate can increase by 30%. Additionally, it reduces scheduling variance by approximately 11 % and 19% respectively, which reduces the cost increase and management difficulties due to processing time variability, improves the stability and efficiency of production scheduling, and ensures a much smoother and more reliable production process.

articleTitle: A2D2: AI-Driven Autonomous Drone-Based Detection Network for Wildfires
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) or drones have promising advantages in wildfire detection, outperforming conventional systems in mobility and versatility. However, current drone operations such as path planning, maneuver control, and data analysis require significant manual work, restricting drone systems' efficiency and effectiveness. To reduce human efforts while improving performance, this paper proposes A2D2, an AI-driven Autonomous Drone-based Detection network, aiming to fully automate the drone operational process for wildfire detection. The proposed system is driven by AI models and automated solutions, including a deep computer vision (DCV) model for wildfire detection, a coverage path planning (CPP) method managing patrol navigation, and a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) model controlling drone's path towards the detected wildfires for inspection. This system programmatically manages the model functions in different stages to ensure autonomous operations with minimal human intervention. This paper describes the design, implementation, and experimental tests of the proposed system, including mathematical analysis and algorithms. The approaches and solutions introduced in this research contribute to the advancements of integrating AI technologies into autonomous drone systems and applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Human-Machine Collaboration Safety Through Personnel Behavior Detection and Separate Speed Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Human-robot collaboration is rapidly advancing, especially in manufacturing, where robots assist with heavy, hazardous, or repetitive tasks. The goal is to enhance productivity while ensuring a safe and efficient work environment. This study explores safety technologies for detecting personnel behavior and monitoring speed and separation, focusing on identifying workers' motion intentions and controlling robots' safety distance with variable speed regulation. This allows robots to manage acceleration and deceleration safely, improving work efficiency and overall production system performance. Using 3D cameras and human posture detection with 34 key points, this research applies the DLOW model for human motion prediction. The DLOW model accurately predicts human movements within 2.5 seconds with an 81.34% accuracy, and these predictions are fed into to the robotic system, which adjusts its movement speed to avoid collisions. A distance-speed relationship model ensures the robot operates at a safe speed based on the worker's position and velocity, reducing harm and resuming normal speed outside the safe zone.

articleTitle: Fast Replanning Slosh-Free Trajectory for Mobile Manipulation Using Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: In this paper, a model predictive control (MPC) framework is proposed to deal with slosh-free liquid transportation task with a mobile manipulator (MM). Two variations of slosh-free trajectroy using MPC with a spherical pendulum model are presented, which are the feedforward and feedback method respectively. The simulation experiments were conducted using a MM combined with a tracked mobile base and a 6-DoF robotic manipulator. The simulated slosh suppression results showed the feedback version of the proposed method goes beyond the existing Trajectory Optimization (TO) based approach by 44% reduction in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), providing a fast re-planning solution for generating a suitable slosh-free motion reference trajectory for a whole-body controlled MM.

articleTitle: Carbon Fiber Robot Manipulator with Virtual Impedance Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental study comparing a robot manipulator's performance constructed with aluminum alloy and carbon fiber components. In addressing safety concerns, we evaluate the collision avoidance strategy known as Virtual Impedance Control. This strategy ensures the safety of both users and the robot itself. By implementing Virtual Impedance Control, the robot adeptly avoids obstacles, contributing to a safer and more reliable robotic operation. These findings underscore the benefits of utilizing carbon fiber in robotic manipulator construction, promising enhanced efficiency and safety.

articleTitle: Diagnostics of Road Conditions Using Acceleration Sensor: Machine Learning - LSTM autoencoder and Gaussian Mixture Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Assessing road conditions is critical in the transportation system to ensure travel safety, mobility and efficiency. In many studies, poor road conditions are detected and analyzed using anomaly detection algorithms, employing supervised and unsupervised learning approaches. The paper presents a novel and low-cost framework using acceleration sensors attached on a vehicle to assess road conditions through machine learning techniques. Two unsupervised machine learning - LSTM autoencoder and GMM-EM models are applied to detect distressed road conditions (i.e., anomaly detection in acceleration data). The sliding window algorithm is utilized along with LSTM autoencoder to filter accelerations and locate patterns of candidate distressed conditions. The magnitude of all accelerations in the vertical, longitudinal, and lateral directions are normalized and transformed into overlapping windows. These windows then serve as input for an LSTM-autoencoder to detect road anomalies. In GMM-EM, all raw acceleration data are used where anomalies are identified when the log probabilities computed from the GMM component are lower than one percentile. Subsequently, all identified anomalies are georeferenced in the ArcGIS software, and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{2}$</tex> value is computed using the identified anomalies and International Roughness Index (IRI). As a result, 77.91% and 82.63 % <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{2}$</tex> values were computed, indicating a strong relationship between the identified poor road conditions using LSTM autoencoder and IRI values. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{2}$</tex> values are 58.89% and 74.35% while using GMM-EM model.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Pole Placement and LQR in Cart Inverted Pendulum Controller Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: The inverted pendulum systems have been well recognized as agreeable benchmarks for evaluating various aspects in control systems. It also mimics numerous real-world important physical systems. Many control algorithms have been implemented for the inverted pendulum system. This paper is presented to conduct the comparative study of the pole placement and linear quadratic regulator (LQR) control designs for the cart inverted pendulum system. The dynamic model of the cart inverted pendulum system, including the belt drive system as an actuator, is modelled. Its linearized model is adopted in the controller design based on the pole placement and LQR methods. Simulations were carried out using the full nonlinear model. The control responses from 5 different controllers designed by the two control techniques are simulated to comprehend the benefits of LQR over the pole placement. The simulation results show higher degrees of freedom in the LQR method in manipulating control performance in the individual states.

articleTitle: Load Side Position Sensorless Control of Robot Manipulators with Flexible Joints
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: One of the most notorious control problems for robot manipulators with flexible joints is vibration during movement, which substantially deteriorates motion accuracy. To cope with this problem, this paper proposes a load side position sensorless control scheme consisting of modified integral sliding mode control, command shaping, and command feedforward. A 2-DOF robot manipulator with flexible joints is used as a simulation platform to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Simulation results indicate that the proposed approach exhibits satisfactory performance.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning in Mixture of Experts Control System for Blind Wheeled-Legged Quadrupedal Locomotion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: The advances in wheeled-legged robots in recent years have led to their proliferation in human environments. However, these robots still face significant challenges regarding non-flat terrain. Stair climbing is particularly difficult for these robots and restricts their functionality in human facilities. We implemented a goal conditioned deep reinforcement learning algorithm to develop a position-based controller that allows Wheely, a wheeled-legged quadrupedal robot, to blindly climb stairs up to a record breaking 10 cm in height or 33% of Wheely's maximum body height. By training the reinforcement learning algorithm on a single environment each time, we create specialized policies that excel at their own specific terrain type. Through the independent training, we create a controller with a mixture of experts architecture that does not need to compromise between different environments, leading to a more optimal policy for each scenario. To maintain robustness, a selector neural network selects the policy based on past observations, allowing the robot to function independently in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Practical Implementation of Q-Learning and Object Detection for Mobile Robot Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Expanding on an earlier study that assessed the performance of a Q-learning approach for solving the path planning problem for mobile robots, this research implemented the RL approach in a real-world setting employing the RoboMas-ter EP Core. The robotic system also included object detection and recognition through the robot's sensors and a pre-trained YOLOv9 model. The robot navigated to predefined target points while avoiding stationary obstacles. The Q-learning algorithm was trained using the Google Colaboratory platform. Experi-ments conducted at various speeds identified an optimal speed and high success rates in obstacle avoidance and target region accuracy were achieved. Additionally, the object detection sys-tem demonstrated strong performance in real-time applications. Despite these successes, challenges such as high friction and multitasking inefficiencies were identified. Future research should address these limitations by enhancing control systems and the robot's multitasking capabilities, as well as using a computer with better processing power to improve overall system performance further.

articleTitle: Wheel Mechanism for Moving on Bumpy Surfaces Using Tensegrity Structure Including Axle Hub
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This research proposes a new wheel design for mobile machines running under bumpy, fragile, and steep slopes such as rocky areas, icy fields, and bumpy off-roads. The wheel is composed of a minimal Tensegrity structure with three rods and an axle hub, which is a part of the Tensegrity structure and passes rotational force onto the wheel. Tensegrity has many unique features, such as deforming as a rubber ball while contacting the external surface with its rigid rod's endpoints, which are helpful as a wheel. The proposed wheel is expected to perform better than the other wheels, such as rubber tires and crawlers, by including the axle hub as a part of the Tensegrity. In this report, we explain the details of the proposed Tensegrity wheel. We also show the results of the experiments of the proposed wheels when actively driven by a motor and when rotated passively. We compared the wheel with a “Wheg” like the proposed wheel except for having no tension and its rods fixed. The results show the high usefulness of proposed Tensegrity wheels including the axel hub in climbing steps.

articleTitle: Propeller Angle Trajectory Analysis of Wall-Climbing Robot with Transition Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm which can be used to optimize the propeller angle trajectory to do maneuvering movement for a wall-climbing robot. The robot implements a double-propeller mechanism with the ability to direct the thrust force exerted by each propeller, with a curve-shaped structure such that it has some free space at the bottom of the robot. With this design, it gives the robot the ability to climb over obstacles during vertical wall-climbing. This research is focused on implementing the algorithm to do transition movement from the ground to wall. To solve the propeller trajectory, this research utilized a data-driven method based on physical simulation environment using genetic algorithm (GA). First, the robot is designed in Simscape environment, incorporating all of the component's inertia, motor speed, and the thrust force exerted by the propellers. Then, the experimental data regarding the noise is also integrated to further improve the simulation's accuracy. After solving the optimization, the result is then tested on the experiment to test the algorithm's performance. The robot is seen to successfully reproduce the intended movement that was done on the simulation, even though that the measurement noise is bigger than expected. However, the robot is still able to perform the movement smoothly. The result and experimental data gathered from this research would be beneficial on the improvements of this robot and for future work regarding obstacle maneuvering of vertical wall-climbing.

articleTitle: Human-Robot Collaboration in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle River Patrol Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: The autonomy of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has significantly influenced research and market development, leading to innovative applications across various fields. However, conventional joystick control methods are still prevalent, presenting operators with challenges related to complexity, limited maneuverability, and multitasking capabilities. To develop a user-friendly and intuitive UAV control system, this paper proposes a vision-based human-robot collaboration system. In this system, the UAV serves as a tool for environmental perception and recognition, while operators take on roles of supervision and decision-making. This study aims to validate the usability of the human-robot collaboration system in real-world river environments. Consequently, we designed two experimental scenarios: river patrol with personnel detection, and riverbank construction site inspection tasks. The UAV employs the Global Positioning System (GPS) for large-scale localization, augmented by visual positioning and semantic segmentation modules to enhance the river tracking model for river patrol. Meanwhile, operators can monitor and semi-automatically adjust flight parameters in real time through a visualization platform.

articleTitle: Enhancing Lifting Efficiency with a Novel Lower-Limb Exosuit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Lifting heavy loads has long posed significant risks, such as lower back pain and injuries due to high compressive forces. To address these challenges, we propose an innovative lower-limb exosuit that integrates both passive and active components, designed to optimize lifting performance while ensuring user comfort and safety. This study evaluates the exosuit's effectiveness in reducing muscle activation and altering the range of motion during squat lifting tasks. Our exosuit leverages a spherical scissor linkage mechanism and elastic bands for hip support, and extension springs for knee support. Experimental evaluation using electromyography (EMG) and motion capture data reveals significant reductions in muscle activity for the rectus femoris and gluteus medius, particularly in the latter, with reductions of 34.6% and 63.2%, respectively. Additionally, substantial changes in joint flexion angles, especially at the ankle were ob. These findings highlight the exosuit's potential to mitigate physical strain and enhance lifting efficiency, paving the way for advancements in assistive technologies for lifting assistance.

articleTitle: The Application of AI Technology in Automated Optical Inspection for System Furniture Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Automatic detection technology has become indispensable in modern industry, capable of meeting the demands for high-value products, shortening production cycles, and addressing labor shortages. Traditional AOI systems face difficulties in establishing accurate detection models and are prone to false positives or negatives, but AI technology promises to solve these problems. This study designed a line scan imaging device, including a line scan camera, a dedicated light source, and a rolling inspection platform, to capture images of board materials and collect data in real-time. We segmented the images into 320x320 pixel local images, collected a large number of normal and defective images, and used CNN to train a recognition model. However, in industrial applications, the model often encounters concept drift issues, leading to performance degradation. To address this problem, we chose the EfficientN etB0 model and compared three methods: full-layer fine-tuning, transfer learning, and the random forest classifier. The results showed that the full-layer fine-tuning method had the highest accuracy but the longest training time, transfer learning reduced training time but had slightly lower accuracy, and the method combining EfficientN etB0 with the random forest classifier had the shortest training time and moderate accuracy. This study applied AI CNN classification combined with AOI preprocessing technology for defect detection in furniture boards and integrated CNN with a random forest classifier to address concept drift issues in real-time, achieving innovative and practical value. Future research will expand to more industries to verify the universality and benefits of this method.

articleTitle: Application of SVR-Based Model for Compensating Comprehensive Thermal Displacement of Machine Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This study develops a detection fixture and method capable of capturing multi-axis thermal errors simultaneously. It can measure thermal errors in the spindle rotation, as well as in the X and Y feed axes, achieving multi-axis synchronous measurement. This approach is more representative of actual machining conditions compared to traditional single-axis experiments and reduces measurement time and costs. Statistical methods are used to separate and analyze thermal errors, with non-linear Support Vector Regression (SVR) employed to establish error models for each axis and position. Compensation is achieved through origin coordinate offset compensation and feed axis pitch error compensation, ensuring comprehensive thermal error compensation for the entire machine. This method enhances the precision and stability of machined parts.

articleTitle: Trajectory and Energy Optimization Method for Industrial Robot Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: The multi-axis energy analysis module is crucial in automated factories, especially when used with robotic arms. We developed a hybrid dynamic model that integrates the dynamics of the multi-axis robot arm with machine learning for error correction, considering the angular velocity and acceleration of each joint. This model provides a mathematical representation of the robot's physical behavior, utilizing angles, velocities, accelerations, and loads for each axis. By incorporating an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with experimental torque values, we estimate the energy consumption for a given trajectory. This hybrid model is used as a surrogate for offline path optimization with the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, formulated as a bi-objective problem focusing on motion time and energy consumption. The PSO algorithm identifies optimal trajectory, velocity, and acceleration settings for the robotic arm to efficiently perform pick-and-place tasks. Experimental evaluations show that this optimization technique can reduce energy consumption by over 10% while maintaining motion speed.

articleTitle: High Precision Positioning through Advanced Robotic Technology Development
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This research focuses on enhancing robotic technology, particularly for achieving high-precision positioning in manual wiring production lines for electronic connectors. This system addresses the needs of customized, small-batch production by incorporating advanced image recognition technologies to boost production accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the robotic arm can achieve a positioning accuracy of up to ±10 µm. Considering the plastic component holes are about 600 µm long and 150 µ m wide, a dual-lens system is employed for precise identification and positioning. A high-resolution 10-megapixel camera is mounted on the robotic arm, utilizing an image positioning technique that adjusts minor movements based on pixel errors between the center and positioning holes. This process ensures that the robotic arm's positioning accuracy is not affected by the repeatability of collaborative robots, achieving a final precision of ±0.01 mm. This technological advancement, facilitated by image processing, allows the robotic arm to align with the plastic component holes precisely, significantly simplifying the terminal insertion process with exceptional accuracy.

articleTitle: Robotic Ultrasonic Forging Technology Applied to Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: The global aerospace industry MRO (maintenance repair overhaul) market size is expected to reach more than 130 billion US dollars in 2032, and robots will play a very important role. Combining robots with additive manufacturing technology to produce large aerospace workpieces can reduce costs. There are already many related research and production examples, such as the manufacturing of rocket barrels. The existing technology cannot avoid the subsequent processing process (grinding), resulting in the manufacturing cost and manufacturing time being unable to be further reduced and shortened. This study introduces a novel method in which robots combine ultrasonic forging and additive manufacturing technology to achieve simultaneous additive manufacturing and shaping of the workpiece appearance. The goal is to meet the required surface roughness specifications of the workpiece and even improve the mechanical properties.

articleTitle: Monocular Visual Odometry Based on Plane Tracking with Rectangular Constraint
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This paper presents a feature-based monocular visual odometry method by detecting and tracking plane of man-made buildings. We utilize the vertical and horizontal structural lines on a plane and rectangular constraint to reconstruct a mesh plane in 3-D space from single 2-D image, tracking the target plane and estimating 6-degree of freedom poses through monocular RGB camera. A reliability testing is integrated, which can reduce the impact of drift and speed up the process through downsampling the input frames. We have evaluated our method through simulation and experiment, The results indicate that our method performs well in noisy environments and can operate in real-time.

articleTitle: Collision-free Motion Policy for Manipulator with Multi-constraint Coordination in Dynamic Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: In human-robot collaboration tasks, the participation of human requires enhanced safety measures for robots. To ensure safety during the execution process, a robotic arm must avoid collisions with any obstacles while approaching the goal position. Therefore, developing an appropriate motion policy is critical for the successful execution of robotic tasks. A comprehensive motion policy for a robotic arm must consider many constraints, such as goal position, goal orientation, static obstacles, dynamic obstacles, and the kinematic limitations of the arm. This paper focuses on integrating multiple constraints to generate motion commands for manipulator. Initially, static obstacles are defined by comparing consecutive point clouds. The information about static obstacles, along with the goal position and orientation of the end effector, is used for global path planning. Each state on the global path is six-dimensional, comprising position and orientation. The global path then serves as a guide for local motion planning, where each state on the global path acts as a local goal. Local motion planning employs the Riemannian Motion Policy (RMP) to integrate subtasks across different dimensions of the task space. These subtasks include approaching the goal position and the goal orientation, collision avoidance, arm joint critical angle constraints, etc. It generates a dynamic motion policy as real-time motion commands for the manipulator. Finally, the end effector reaches the target safely. The motion policy for the robotic arm in this paper is validated in both simulated and real-world environments. It is successfully applied to scenarios involving both static and dynamic obstacles and completes the assigned tasks safely.

articleTitle: Human Motion Tracking: A Comparative Analysis of Recent Advancements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This paper explores the advancements in human motion-tracking technology within the past three years, analyzing research that presents novel methods for capturing and analyzing human movement. We examine the methodologies employed by each approach, including sensor-based systems, radar technology, Wi-Fi signal utilization, lightweight networks for real-time action recognition, and a system for joint camera localization and human motion tracking. This paper compares each surveyed research's advantages, disadvantages, and limitations, highlighting their practical implications and potential applications. Finally, this review discusses the future directions and challenges within human motion tracking.

articleTitle: State Estimation for Autonomous Surface Vehicles: A Neural Network-Assisted Observer Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) have emerged as a revolutionary solution to enhance search and rescue (SAR) operations in open waters. In order to successfully do SAR missions, the ability of the boat to autonomously perform exploration with accurate movements is crucial. This paper presents a method to accurately track a boat's movement only based on the boat's kinematic equation. To implement this method, a neural-network is implemented by training it with the real robot's movement coordinate. In this research, a boat prototype is designed and to track the boat's movement, a vision-based tracking method is implemented by using a drone. A video of the boat's movement is captured from above, then the robot's moving coordinate is extracted by utilizing OpenCV object tracking. By integrating the boat's kinematic equation with a trained neural-network to compensate for the dynamic uncertainties present in the physical world, the robot's movement can be accurately tracked even without the help of any sensor. There are a lot of uncertainties that present in the water, thus large set of data is needed to further improve the robot's performance. This paper serves as a preliminary study on whether a neural-network could be utilized for movement tracking of a boat. To further improve the robot's movement tracking ability, more sensors could be utilized with added control system for position tracking ability.

articleTitle: A Rigid-Soft Switchable Lower Body Exosuit for Lifting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: Lower-limb assistive wearable exosuits can reduce occupational injuries of manual workers by assisting strenuous and repetitive lifting tasks. This study aims to develop a lower-limb assistive wearable exosuit using a mechanism called SwitchSpring to assist users during lifting. The base structure of the SwitchSpring functions as a spring rod and can switch between rigid and soft states by adjusting the cable tension on the rod. When the SwitchSpring is switched to its rigid state, the energy is harvested and released as the user squats down and stands up. The lower limb joint angles and muscle activations of a female subject lifting a 5 kg box with and without the device were measured. The results show that the SwitchSpring wearable robot manages to reduce the muscle activation level by up to 30% on the rectus femoris (RF), 35% on the biceps femoris (BF), and 37% on the tibialis anterior (TA), showing the potential of lower limb power assistance in lifting.

articleTitle: Advanced Techniques for Maritime Target Detection and Recognition Using YOLO-v7 and Sliding Window Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced methodology for maritime target identification utilising the latest YOLO-v7 object detection algorithm and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The study integrates sliding window segmentation and Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) techniques to enhance detection accuracy in complex maritime environments. Various preprocessing techniques, including image augmentation and standardisation, are applied to publicly accessible maritime databases and imagery captured by the Albatross II UAV. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in detection precision, leveraging deep learning techniques to address challenges posed by variable weather conditions and diverse object sizes. Experimental results indicate that the enhanced YOLO-v7 algorithm combined with sliding window segmentation increases detection accuracy by 1-2%.

articleTitle: Mixed Reality Robot Programming Using Hand Gestures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: In this paper, we present a hand gesture-based robot path generation system using mixed reality (MR) for interactive robot programming. A hand-gesture recognition scheme is proposed to recognize specific gestures for path generation and modification. A user can intuitively plan a virtual path by hand gestures in the actual working space and send the planned path to the robot controller to execute through the MR glasses. A human-machine interface is designed to allow a user to assign the required task and send control commands to the robot. To ensure the robot can accurately move along the planned path, a calibration procedure is designed to establish the relationship between the MR system and robot navigation system. The proposed method has been realized and verified using a TM5 cobot and HoloLens II. The experimental results show that the robot navigation error is within 2mm using the developed MR-based robot programming system.

articleTitle: Larva-Inspired Drilling Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This study aims to develop a drilling robot designed to overcome the complexities of underground environments. The robot's structure includes a specially designed drill, a bio-inspired three-segment steering mechanism, and a track system with propulsion capabilities. The experimental environment uses a mixture of fine sand and water to simulate stable soil properties. Actual operational data have been used to estimate the range of torque required for drilling.

articleTitle: Achieving Continuous Bouncing Through Resonance-Driven Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to robotic jumping mechanisms utilizing resonance principles to maximize vertical height. We introduce a two-mass system with springs and mass transfer, driven by an oscillating weight to achieve resonance-enhanced jumping performance. Through detailed mathematical modeling and Matlab simulations, we optimize system parameters to maintain the driving frequency near the natural resonance, thereby improving energy efficiency. A phys-ical prototype was constructed to validate the simulation results, with jump heights measured using Tracker image software. Experimental data closely matched simulations at a motor-driving frequency of 22.92 rad/s and a damping ratio of 2, despite minor initial discrepancies. The mechanism demonstrates consistent and effective jumping performance, outperforming traditional spring-based and pneumatic actuators. We discuss future enhancements, including adjustable spring constants and revised linkage systems, to adapt to diverse environments and achieve higher driving frequencies. This research contributes to the field of mobile robotics by offering a versatile solution for obstacle traversal and enhanced mobility in challenging terrains, with potential applications in search and rescue, military operations, and industrial scenarios.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Automated Nasal Swab Robots by Integrating Visual Detection and Compliance Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test is widely used to confirm COVID-19 infection, and it must be performed by medical workers according to regulations, exposing them to a high risk of infection. In this paper, we design and implement an automated nasal swab robot to replace medical workers in performing PCR tests. The proposed robot consists of a depth camera for nostril detection and nasal passage estimation, and a 6-axis industrial robot with a force/torque sensor to implement compliance control for safe nasal swabbing. Experiments verify that the vision system works satisfactorily while the compliance control law allows the robot to regulate the contact force within a prescribed level. Therefore, safe and automated nasal swab is accomplished by the proposed robot.

articleTitle: Path Planning and Control of a 6-DOF Manipulator for Freeform Surface Polishing Based-on a Point Cloud Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel path generation method for robotic surface polishing based on point cloud data. In this method, an initial path is first planned to create waypoints via the point cloud. The method estimates the contact area to dynamically adjust initial path points to ensure uniform trajectory coverage on the surface. In this paper, the bilateral tool path generation (BTPG) algorithm is proposed based on a dual-thread strategy to expedite polishing path generation. Further, we introduce a method that generates smooth postures to enhance the stability of the robotic polishing pose. In this work, hybrid force/velocity control scheme is adopted to track polishing path and apply the assigned force on the workpiece freeform surface. Practical experimental results show that the proposed method achieves 95% improvement in path planning time and 85% in smoothness of the robot fourth joint's posture compared with the baseline slicing method.
